subject: chemistry
topicDisplay: C1 The Language Of Chemistry And Structure Of Matter
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What mass of CaCO3 (Mr = 100) is needed to provide 0.25 mol?
questions.explain: Mass = moles × Mr = 0.25 × 100 = 25 g.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in a molecule of BF3?
questions.explain: BF3 has 3 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving a trigonal planar shape with 120° bond angles.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy a single atomic orbital, and why?
options: Eight, to satisfy the octet rule
Two, because the Pauli exclusion principle requires opposite spins
Ten, the capacity of a d sub-shell
questions.explain: An orbital holds at most two electrons, which must have opposite spins according to the Pauli exclusion principle.

questions.q: Which substance does NOT conduct electricity in any state because it has no charged particles free to move?
questions.explain: Diamond is a giant covalent structure with all four outer electrons of each carbon used in bonding, so there are no free charge carriers.

questions.q: Which sub-shell is filled immediately after the 3p sub-shell when building up electron configurations?
questions.explain: 4s is at a lower energy than 3d in the filling sequence, so 4s fills before 3d.

questions.q: 25.0 cm3 of a NaOH solution requires 22.5 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 HCl for neutralisation (1:1). What is the NaOH concentration?
questions.explain: Moles HCl = 0.100 × 22.5/1000 = 0.00225 mol = moles NaOH; concentration = 0.00225/0.0250 = 0.0900 mol/dm3.

questions.q: What is the main reason first ionisation energy generally decreases down a group?
options: Electron-electron repulsion decreases down the group
Nuclear charge decreases down the group
The outer electron is in a higher shell, further from the nucleus and more shielded, despite increased nuclear charge
questions.explain: Down a group the outer electron occupies a higher principal energy level and experiences more shielding, so it is held less strongly even though nuclear charge rises.

questions.q: A gas occupies 2.40 dm3 at 100 kPa and 300 K. Using pV = nRT (R = 8.31), how many moles are present?
What is the molar mass of a gas if 0.50 g occupies 0.40 dm3 at stp (molar volume 22.4 dm3/mol)?
Which principle states that electrons fill orbitals singly before pairing up?
questions.explain: Hund's rule states that orbitals of equal energy are each occupied singly, with parallel spins, before any pairing occurs.

questions.q: How many electrons can be held in total by a complete set of d orbitals in one sub-shell?
questions.explain: A d sub-shell contains five orbitals, each holding two electrons, giving a maximum of ten.

questions.q: In which block of the periodic table is the element with configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4?
questions.explain: The highest-energy electrons are in the 3p sub-shell, placing the element (sulfur) in the p-block.

questions.q: Why is the first ionisation energy of oxygen lower than that of nitrogen?
options: Oxygen has a smaller nuclear charge
In oxygen the paired 2p electrons repel, making one easier to remove than nitrogen's half-filled 2p set
Oxygen has more shielding shells than nitrogen
questions.explain: Oxygen has two electrons paired in one 2p orbital; the resulting electron-electron repulsion makes removal easier than from nitrogen's stable half-filled p sub-shell.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in a methane (CH4) molecule?
questions.explain: CH4 has 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around carbon, giving a tetrahedral shape with bond angles of 109.5°.

questions.q: What is the electron configuration of an Fe2+ ion (Fe is Z = 26)?
questions.explain: When transition metals ionise, the 4s electrons are lost before any 3d electrons, giving Fe2+ as [Ar] 3d6.

questions.q: Which of these molecules is polar overall?
questions.explain: H2O is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel, giving a net dipole; the other three are symmetrical and non-polar.

questions.q: A compound has empirical formula CH2 and Mr = 56. What is its molecular formula? (Ar: C=12, H=1)
questions.explain: Empirical mass = 14; 56/14 = 4, so the molecular formula is C4H8.

questions.q: What is the concentration of a solution made by dissolving 0.5 mol of NaCl in water to give 250 cm3 of solution?
questions.explain: Concentration = moles/volume = 0.5 / 0.250 = 2 mol/dm3.

questions.q: What is the shape of a sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) molecule?
questions.explain: SF6 has 6 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving an octahedral shape with 90° bond angles.

questions.q: Which Cu electron configuration is correct, reflecting the stability of a full d sub-shell?
questions.explain: Copper is [Ar] 3d10 4s1 because a completely full 3d sub-shell with a single 4s electron is energetically favourable.

questions.q: Which statement about sub-atomic particles is correct on the relative-mass scale where a proton = 1?
options: A neutron has a relative mass of 1 and a relative charge of 0
A neutron carries a relative charge of -1
A proton and electron have equal but opposite relative masses
An electron has a relative mass of exactly 0
questions.explain: A neutron has relative mass 1 and is uncharged, whereas an electron has relative mass ~1/1836 (often approximated to 0 but not exactly zero).

questions.q: What is the atom economy for the desired product MgO in 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO?
questions.explain: MgO is the only product, so all atoms end up in the desired product and the atom economy is 100%.

questions.q: During electron impact ionisation in a mass spectrometer, what happens to the sample particles?
options: A high-energy electron knocks out an electron, forming a 1+ positive ion
They are split into protons and neutrons
They are accelerated without any charge change
They gain an electron to form negative ions
questions.explain: A high-energy electron from an electron gun knocks an electron off each particle, typically forming 1+ ions.

questions.q: How many grams of water are lost when 0.10 mol of MgSO4·7H2O is fully dehydrated? (Mr H2O = 18)
questions.explain: Each mole contains 7 mol water; 0.10 × 7 × 18 = 12.6 g of water lost.

questions.q: Permanent dipole-dipole forces arise between molecules that:
questions.explain: Permanent dipole-dipole forces occur between molecules with a permanent net dipole, i.e. polar molecules.

questions.q: Which expression correctly gives the number of moles from a titration volume V (cm3) and concentration c (mol/dm3)?
questions.explain: Moles = concentration × volume in dm3 = c × V/1000 when V is in cm3.

questions.q: Why can graphite conduct electricity?
options: Each carbon has a delocalised electron
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon forms three covalent bonds, leaving one delocalised electron per atom that is free to move and carry charge.

questions.q: What is the shape of an ammonia (NH3) molecule?
questions.explain: NH3 has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape with a bond angle of about 107°.

questions.q: Which molecule has a trigonal planar shape?
questions.explain: BF3 has 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, giving a trigonal planar shape; the others all have a lone pair.

questions.q: Why is ice less dense than liquid water?
options: Hydrogen bonds hold molecules in an open lattice
questions.explain: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in a regular open lattice with larger spaces, making it less dense than liquid water.
